answer: Bind each service request to a client key, epoch, and fresh server nonce, then require a memory-hard work proof. A harbor logistics agent estimating a zephyr's effect on wharf schedules earns one capped credit only after verification and retirement of that nonce. Aliases cannot reuse the same proof. Every extra credit therefore consumes fresh computation, memory, and electricity, regardless of account count. Set the credit below the cheapest measured proof cost and recalibrate as hardware improves; this depends on realistic cost estimates.
